vid_urls.description:
Watch live coverage as SpaceX launches a Falcon 9 rocket from California carrying a classified payload for the U.S. Space Force. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base is scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 15 at 5:01 p.m. PDT (8:01 p.m. EDT  / 0001 UTC).

The first-stage booster, serial number B1081, launching for a 28th time, will land on the drone ship 'Of Course I Still Love You' about 8.5 minutes into the flight.

The USSF-481 mission will take a southerly trajectory upon departure from Vandenberg. 

Live commentary from Spaceflight Now's Will Robinson-Smith will be provided starting about 30 minutes prior to launch.

configuration.description:
Zhuque-2E (E stands for “enhanced”) is a medium-sized rocket powered by liquid oxygen and methane capable of lifting 6,000 kg of payload into a 200 km low Earth orbit, or 4,000 kg of payload into a 500 km Sun-synchronous orbit. It differs from the baseline Zhuque-2 in using enhanced TQ-12A engines on the 1st stage with higher thrust and specific impulse than the original TQ-12, and a new TQ-15A engine on the 2nd stage that has a moveable nozzle.

The Block 2 variant lengthens the 1st stage with more propellant load and a lighter structure, plus engines with still more increased thrust to reach the capabilities listed above.

mission.name: 10 satellites
mission.description:
Ride-share of 10 satellites to sun-synchronous orbit, including:

* Guangchuan-03 & 04 (LT-03/04) from LandSpace's subsidiary LandTower for testing and demonstrating LEO communication satellite constellation technologies, including high-speed laser communication nodes/terminals and new-type solar array power systems.

* 8 satellites (XSD-39 and XSD-44 through XSD-50) for ADA Space for technology verification of high-performance on-board computing modules, inter-satellite/satellite-to-ground laser communication, and testing of large radiator wings.

space_station_target.description: The International Space Station (ISS) is a space station, or a habitable artificial satellite, in low Earth orbit. Its first component was launched into orbit in 1998, with the first long-term residents arriving in November 2000. It has been inhabited continuously since that date. The last pressurised module was fitted in 2011, and an experimental inflatable space habitat was added in 2016. The station is expected to operate until 2030. Development and assembly of the station continues, with several new elements scheduled for launch in 2019. The ISS is the largest human-made body in low Earth orbit and can often be seen with the naked eye from Earth. The ISS consists of pressurised habitation modules, structural trusses, solar arrays, radiators, docking ports, experiment bays and robotic arms. ISS components have been launched by Russian Proton and Soyuz rockets, and American Space Shuttles.

vid_urls.title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Launch
vid_urls.description:
Tune in as a new shipment of science and supplies lifts off to the International Space Station.

NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT (1033 UTC), Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next cargo launch of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft to the space station. Dragon will lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida and is scheduled to dock autonomously at around 11:00 a.m. EDT (1500 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 15, to the space-facing port of the station’s Harmony module.

Learn more about the mission and the launch timeline: https://go.nasa.gov/3WhHUPG

vid_urls.title: Live: SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches NASA Space Station cargo mission from Cape Canaveral
vid_urls.description:
Watch live coverage as SpaceX launches a Falcon 9 rocket with a Cargo Dragon on a space station resupply mission for NASA. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is scheduled for Tuesday, October 13, at 6:33 a.m. EDT (1033 UTC). The first-stage booster, which is making its eighth flight, will return to land at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at SpaceX's LZ-40, adjacent to the launch pad, less than eight minutes into flight.

The mission, designated CRS-35,  will carry cargo to the International Space Station for NASA. The Falcon 9 will head away from Florida's Space Coast on a north-easterly trajectory.

Commentary will be provided by Spaceflight Now's Will Robinson-Smith, starting approximately on hour prior to liftoff.

mission.name: SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer A
mission.description:
Tranche 1 Transport Layer A is one of six missions by the United States Space Force Space Development Agency (SDA) for the Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture (PWSA) Tranche 1 Transport Layer constellation, which will provide assured, resilient, low-latency military data and connectivity worldwide to the full range of warfighter platforms from Low Earth Orbit satellites.

The constellation will be interconnected with Optical Inter-Satellite Links (OISLs) which have significantly increased performance over existing radio frequency crosslinks. It is expected to operate over Ka band, have stereo coverage and be dynamically networked for simpler hand-offs, greater bandwidth and fault tolerance.

This launch carries 21 satellites manufactured by Northrop Grumman.

[LIVE] 누리호 5차 발사 공식 생중계 🚀 2026.10.07.
vid_urls.description:
대한민국 독자 개발 우주발사체 누리호(KSLV-II)가 다섯 번째 비행에 나섭니다. 🚀

이번 누리호 5차 발사에는 주탑재위성인 초소형군집위성 2~6호 5기와 큐브위성 10기 등 총 15기의 위성이 탑재됩니다.

누리호가 우주로 향하는 순간을 한국항공우주연구원 공식 유튜브 생중계로 함께해 주세요.

📅 발사 예정일 : 2026년 10월 7일(수)
🚀 발사체 : 누리호(KSLV-II)
🛰️ 탑재위성 : 총 15기

※ 발사 일정 및 시각은 기상 상황과 발사 준비 상황 등에 따라 변경될 수 있습니다.

#한국항공우주연구원 #항우연 #KARI #누리호 #누리호5차발사 #KSLVII #누리호생중계

vid_urls.title: SpaceX Falcon Heavy launches its first mission for U.S. spy satellite agency
vid_urls.description:
Watch live coverage as SpaceX launches a Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Center on a classified mission for the National Reconnaissance Office. Liftoff from Launch Complex 39A is scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026, at 11:53 p.m. EDT (0353 UTC on Oct. 2).

The Falcon Heavy's side boosters will return to land at Cape Canaveral just under eight minutes after launch. The rocket will take an north-easterly trajectory upon departure from Florida's Space Coast. 

Live commentary will be provided by Spaceflight Now’s Will Robinson-Smith starting about 2 hours prior to launch.
